children: Nvidia's board, which the Journal has reported is preparing to oust the company's founder, has 11 members. One is Huang himself.
In the absence of a chair (a trait shared by 1% of other publicly traded U.S. companies), the board has a lead director, Stephen Neal.

Neal, a trial attorney, is former CEO of law firm Cooley, where he remains chairman emeritus. He's been on the board of Nvidia since 2019. His duties include presiding over board meetings when Huang isn't present, and acting as a conduit between board members and the CEO "on sensitive issues," according to Nvidia.
Here are the other nine directors:
Tench Coxe, former managing director of Sutter Hill Ventures
John O. Dabiri, aeronautics and engineering professor at the California Institute of Technology
Dawn Hudson, a former NFL and Pepsi-Cola executive
Harvey C. Jones, managing partner at Square Wave Ventures
Melissa B. Lora, former president of Taco Bell
A. Brooke Seawell, venture partner at New Enterprise Associates
Aarti Shah, a former Eli Lilly executive
Mark A. Stevens, managing partner at S-Cubed Capital
Suzanne Nora Johnson, former vice chairman at Golden Sachs
In its 2026 annual report, Nvidia said it believed the structure was to the benefit of shareholders, "without the need to appoint a person to serve as chairperson of the board."
As Nvidia sheds hundreds of billions of dollars in market value, investors appear to have realized a few more checks on the powerful CEO wouldn't have gone amiss.
